Theme

Latin word

summus

summus, summa, summum

adjective, superlative of superus · Declension on Wiktionary

utmost, greatest (in degree); highest, utmost: the maximum (of speed, effort, volume); the top of; the top of, the surface of; the top of: the top of the tree, the top of the hill; utmost, total, complete (of degree)

In this lexicon

  • extreme

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.33: summum jūs summa injūria; Cic. Rep. 1.1: ad summam senectūtem, to extreme old age (Lewis & Short)

  • maximum

    also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.3.7: summā vōce, at the top of his voice (Lewis & Short); Traupman 110: summā vōce; Traupman 396

  • on top of

    also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.48: in summā columnā (Lewis & Short, s.v. superus); Caes. BG 1.22: summus mōns (Lewis & Short); Traupman 396

  • surface

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Cas. 2.6.33: in aquā summā natāre (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fin. 4.64: ad aquam summam appropinquāre (Lewis & Short)

  • the top of

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 2.13.11: in summā Sacrā viā; Traupman 396

  • top

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 396

  • total

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Agr. 1.21: summa tranquillitās pācis et ōtiī (Lewis & Short); Cic. Imp. Pomp. 44: ex summā inopiā (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 4.17: summa difficultās

  • amīcus summus (amīca summa): friend

    classical
